<section class="about-section">

      <div class="about-text">
        <p>
          <strong>Human in the loop:</strong> Dieter Olson.
        </p>

        <p>
          This site collects research notes and analysis on the biomechanics of the golf swing and related topics in multibody dynamics and control theory.
        </p>

        <p>
          My name is Dieter Olson. I am a chemical engineer by training and manage an R&amp;D facility specializing in plasma arc gasification and thermal treatment of waste materials. The facility converts waste feedstocks into synthesis gas at temperatures exceeding 5000 K.
        </p>

        <p>
          I have long been interested in the science behind the golf swing and the application of engineering principles to biomechanics. That interest took me through the golf biomechanics literature—the foundational work of Cochran &amp; Stobbs (1968), Jorgensen (1970), and Nesbit (2005)—and through control theory texts by Isidori, Tedrake, and Murray et al. From there I began applying nonlinear control theory and multibody dynamics to the swing. See the <a href="../resources/bibliography.html">Bibliography</a> for the full reference list.
        </p>

        <p>
          My research interests include robotics control, multibody modeling, parallel mechanisms, and the interaction of passive dynamics with active control—the namesake of this website. The central question: how much of observed motion can be attributed to the system's autonomous dynamics (drift) versus active muscular input (control)?
        </p>

        <p>
          For questions, feedback, or collaboration inquiries, please contact me via email at <a href="mailto:dieterolson@AffineDrift.com">dieterolson@AffineDrift.com</a>.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
